newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Greens say they undermined on labour law.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Greens say they undermined on labour law.

text.p: Greens senator Dee Margetts said on Thursday the Australian Democrats support for the government's labour law reforms would undermine the Greens proposed amendments.

"Unfortunately, the government has secured support for the fundamentals of this bill from the Australian Democrats and we can only attempt to make the best of a bad situation for workers in this country," Margetts said in a statement.
Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith is currently negotiating with the Democrats in the hope of winning their support for the Workplace Relations Bill.
The Greens on Thursday released 80 amendments opposing further deregulation of the labour market.
Margetts said: "Further deregulation of industrial relations and the move to individual contracts is designed to please corporate Australia by 'greater flexibility in the workplace'."
"It involves a substantial power shift which will inevitably lead to greater inequity than already exists in this country."
The bill will be debated in the upper house of parliament, the Senate, next week.
The government needs two extra votes to pass any legislation in the Senate, where it does not have a clear majority, and all other non-government parties are opposed to the legislation.
